records.title: Decompression Sickness in the F/A-18C After Atypical Cabin Pressure Fluctuations
records.author: Lee KJ, Sanou AZ
records.locator: Case Reports 1 and 2, pp. 479–480 and Figure 2

case_facts.case_notes: Aircraft altitude at the event was 600 ft on a carrier approach. The cabin was overpressurized before abrupt decompression. The peak cabin overpressure was not quantified.
Aircraft at 30,000 ft. Cabin pressure altitude fluctuated from 11,000 to 18,000 ft and then to 9,000 ft. The figure provides a trace illustration and no machine-readable trace.

observations.outcome_window: Substernal discomfort and cough five minutes after landing. Reevaluation at 20 hours after the event led to hyperbaric treatment. No recurrence was reported during a 14-day grounding period.
observations.note: Two selected clinician-diagnosed Type II DCS episodes. The affected exposure population and incident dates were not given.

observations.outcome_window: Initial in-flight chest symptoms. First flight-surgeon evaluation 90 minutes after the event. Later neurological deficits off oxygen prompted confirmation of the clinical DCS diagnosis. Return to flying after 14 days of observation.
